evals.name: laptop-screen-read
evals.prompt: what's on my laptop screen right now? is there any error or warning showing anywhere on it?
evals.expected_output: A description of what is on the primary display, from a winshot capture of that display only, with every printed tile read.
assertions: Captured with winshot, not PowerShell / System.Windows.Forms / another tool
Captured only the laptop (primary) display, not the whole desktop
Wrote the capture under /tmp or a scratch dir, not the current directory
Read every image path winshot printed
The answer names the application(s) visible and says whether an error or warning is showing

evals.name: capcut-window-details
evals.prompt: check CapCut for me - what's the name of the project that's open, and how long is the audio clip on the timeline?
evals.expected_output: The CapCut project name and the clip duration, from a winshot capture of the CapCut window (not a whole-desktop capture).
assertions: Captured with winshot, not PowerShell / System.Windows.Forms / another tool
Targeted the CapCut window (--window, --exe or an hwnd), not a whole display or desktop
Wrote the capture under /tmp or a scratch dir, not the current directory
Read every image path winshot printed
The answer gives a project name and a clip duration

evals.name: save-second-monitor-raw
evals.prompt: grab a full-resolution screenshot of my second monitor and save it to C:\Users\plafayette\Pictures\winshot-skill-test\<name>.png so I can look at it later
evals.expected_output: One lossless PNG of DISPLAY5 at its physical 1920x1080, at exactly the requested path.
assertions: A PNG exists at exactly the requested path
The saved PNG is the second monitor at full physical resolution (1920x1080)
Used winshot --raw (one lossless file), so no tiles or downscaled copy were saved instead
